spec.name: Trend v5
spec.notes: Twelve-month return skipping the most recent weeks, long the strongest fifth.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.6, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 10%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.63 to 1.64 (change +0.01).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.63 to 1.63. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.59 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.63); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is -0.42 against 1.63 as submitted; the strategy never saw 139 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.23 against 1.63 in research, a gap of +1.86.
The best year gives 22% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 152%; Sharpe is 3.43 in calm and -3.21 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.15, so the claimed 1.60 becomes 1.45 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.67 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.53).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.63 to as low as 1.01 (as low as 1.15 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (21 days) give 29% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 35% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (survivorship_test EX-4, holdout_test EX-5).
